faq:faq-wor-021.title: What is zakat al-fitr and do I have to pay it?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1503: zakat al-fitr is due on every Muslim, young or old, and is given before the Eid prayer
Says it was set as one sa' of food, roughly 3 kg of a staple food; Canadian masjids announce a cash amount each year
Differences: schools differ on cash or food; a convert owes it only if Muslim when it became due

faq:faq-sup-006.title: When should I get professional help instead of just talking to friends or an imam?
keyPoints: Says get professional help if sadness or anxiety lasts weeks, disrupts sleep, eating, work or study, or with thoughts of self-harm
Gives 9-1-1 for immediate danger, then 9-8-8 by call or text any time for thoughts of suicide
Gives ConnexOntario 1-866-531-2600 or text CONNEX to 247247 (Ontario only) and mentions Muslim counsellors

faq:faq-sup-008.title: What number do I call in a mental health crisis in Canada?
keyPoints: Gives 9-1-1 for immediate danger, then 9-8-8 by call or text any time, in English or French, for thoughts of suicide
Gives Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868 (under 30) and Hope for Wellness 1-855-242-3310
Says 741741 is a US text number and not the Canadian service

faq:faq-sup-009.title: Someone I met at the masjid asked me for money. What should I do?
keyPoints: Says you never have to give money and a good community will not pressure a new Muslim to pay
Advises giving charity to a registered organisation, not an individual, by traceable payment, not cash or gift cards (CRA)
Advises telling someone at the masjid office and reporting scams to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre

faq:faq-sup-010.title: How can I check that a fundraiser or charity is real?
keyPoints: Advises checking a charity's registration number on the CRA list of charities or by calling the CRA at 1-800-267-2384
Lists warning signs: rushing, cash, gift cards or crypto, lookalike names, free email addresses and fake crowdfunding pages

faq:faq-sup-011.title: Someone online wants to marry me very quickly. Is that a red flag?
keyPoints: Lists CAFC romance-fraud signs: love before meeting, moving chats private, never meeting, asking for money, isolating you
Says never send money or personal documents to someone you have not met
Says a sincere suitor involves family, friends or a trusted imam; refers the religious side of marriage to a local imam

faq:faq-sup-013.title: Someone offered to help with my immigration or sponsorship. How do I know it is not a scam?
keyPoints: Says IRCC states no one can guarantee approval or faster processing
Lists what IRCC will never do: personal bank account, private transfer, Gmail/Hotmail/Yahoo, payment by phone, social media contact
Advises reporting through IRCC's page, CAFC and police, and using a licensed immigration lawyer or consultant

faq:faq-sup-015.title: How do I report abuse by an imam, teacher or someone at a Muslim organisation?
keyPoints: Says in Ontario everyone is required by law to report a child who may be at risk to a children's aid society
Advises 9-1-1 in immediate danger, police for crimes, the organisation's board, and the CRA for misuse of charity money
Says mentors or groups linked to Revert Guide can be reported through the get help page

faq:faq-sup-016.title: A group says most Muslims are not real Muslims and wants me to cut off my family. Should I worry?
keyPoints: Says a group calling most Muslims not real Muslims and urging you to cut off family is a warning sign
Cites Public Safety Canada on recruiters isolating people (Daesh example) and saying violent extremism is not linked to any religion
Gives 9-1-1 if violence is mentioned and ETA 416-617-4561 (GTA and Southern Ontario) for worries about isolation or extremism

faq:faq-sup-017.title: I have not told my family I am Muslim yet. How can I keep safe?
keyPoints: Says when to tell family is the reader's own decision
Warns apps, browser history and messages can be seen and cannot surely be erased; advises strong passwords and two-step sign-in
Points to the Government of Canada safety planning guide and 9-1-1 in danger

faq:faq-sup-018.title: I think I have been scammed. Who do I tell?
keyPoints: Says stop sending money, report to local police first, then to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre
Gives CAFC phone 1-888-495-8501, Monday to Friday 10 am to 4:45 pm Eastern, closed on holidays
Says being scammed is not your fault

faq:faq-sup-019.title: If I contact a helpline, will they tell my family?
keyPoints: Says helplines keep conversations private and do not contact your family just because you called
Says Kids Help Phone calls are confidential and anonymous, while texts are confidential but not anonymous
Says staff may contact emergency services or child protection if someone's life is in danger

faq:faq-lrn-008.title: Which Muslim apps are safe for my privacy?
keyPoints: Says 2020 reporting found Muslim Pro sent users' location data to a data broker; the company denies giving data to the military
Says Muslim Pro's current privacy policy still allows sharing some data with advertisers (confirm it is still current)
Recommends Pillars (location stays on phone, no ads) and Quran.com (no sale of data, no account needed, uses Google Analytics)

faq:faq-sup-020.title: Can Revert Guide help me if I am struggling with my mental health?
keyPoints: Says Revert Guide is not a counselling service or a substitute for professional care, and nobody monitors messages in real time
Gives 9-1-1 if in danger, then 9-8-8 by call or text at any time for thoughts of suicide

faq:faq-wor-022.title: Do I have to pay zakat as a new Muslim?
keyPoints: Says zakat is 2.5 percent of certain assets held above the nisab for a full lunar year (hawl, about 354 days)
Says nothing is owed for years before Islam; a Shafi'i SeekersGuidance answer counts the first zakat year from the day of Shahada
Says the nisab is set by gold or silver and charities use different gram figures; cites Bukhari 1395 and 1405

faq:faq-wor-023.title: Do I pay zakat on my RRSP or TFSA?
keyPoints: Says NZF Canada counts accessible RRSP/TFSA funds at their value on the zakat date, subtracting withdrawal tax for an RRSP
Differences: scholars count the accessible value, the underlying assets, or wait until withdrawal
Also cites the Muslim Welfare Canada zakat calculator, whose source entry is still review-needed

faq:faq-wor-024.title: Do my debts, like a student loan or car loan, reduce my zakat?
keyPoints: Says debts due soon can often be subtracted before working out zakat, depending on the scholar
Says some Canadian calculators subtract only the coming year's payments on long-term debts like a mortgage
Only source is the Muslim Welfare Canada calculator (review-needed); differences: deduct all debts, this year's only, or none

faq:faq-wor-025.title: Where should I give my zakat, and how do I avoid charity scams?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 9:60: zakat goes to eight named groups, starting with the poor and the needy
Advises giving via a local masjid or a registered Canadian charity with a zakat policy, checking its registration with the CRA
Warns against high-pressure requests, crypto-only payments and crowdfunding pages you cannot verify

faq:faq-wor-026.title: I am a new Muslim struggling with money. Can I receive zakat?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 9:60: the poor, the needy and 'those whose hearts are attracted to the faith', which some Canadian charities apply to new Muslims
Says NZF Canada accepts zakat applications from Muslims in financial hardship
Differences: scholars differ on whether the 'hearts attracted' category still applies today
Advises sharing personal details only through an organisation's official application

faq:faq-lif-031.title: I became Muslim and my boyfriend, girlfriend or partner is not. What do I do now?
keyPoints: Says the Shahada is valid while in a relationship, and sexual intimacy must stop because it belongs inside marriage (Quran 17:32)
Says scholars state as consensus that a Muslim woman does not marry a non-Muslim man (Quran 2:221, AMJA fatwa 21783)
Says a Muslim man may marry a chaste Christian or Jewish woman (Quran 5:5); AMJA advises against it; Shafi'i conditions are stricter
Advises planning with a lawyer and local services before anyone moves out if sharing a home, children or money

faq:faq-lif-032.title: My father is not Muslim. Who is my wali?
keyPoints: Says a non-Muslim father is not the wali in the nikah and his permission is not needed (SeekersGuidance, April 2025)
Cites AMJA Family Code art. 19: with no Muslim paternal relatives, a community-appointed, state-licensed person or a delegated Muslim man acts
Differences: Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali require a wali (Abu Dawud 2085); Hanafi allows her own contract; AMJA 87635 advises repeating it
Warns against a stranger or the suitor's friend offering to be wali in a hurry

faq:faq-sup-021.title: I am under 18 and my parents do not know I am Muslim. What should I do?
keyPoints: Says a minor's Shahada is valid and they can practise quietly: believe, make dua, pray where they can (SeekersGuidance 2023)
Advises staying kind and honest with parents, not running away, and never keeping secrets with an adult who asks to hide chats
Gives Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868 if unsafe at home, then 911 in danger (911 is listed second)

faq:faq-lif-033.title: My job involves serving alcohol, handling pork or interest. Do I have to quit right away?
keyPoints: Says direct roles (serving or selling alcohol, preparing pork) are not allowed but indirect ones (cleaning, general till) are (Hanafi answers)
Cites a Hanafi answer: if quitting means not paying rent or basics, keep working while actively seeking permissible work
Gives no interest-specific ruling though the question asks; AMJA 22421 (direct interest-based credit work not allowed) is only in sources
Says Ontario's human rights creed policy gives examples of a coworker taking over specific tasks

faq:faq-lif-048.title: Can I have a one-to-one meeting with a colleague of the opposite sex?
keyPoints: Defines khalwa as being alone in a closed place others cannot see into or enter (Hanafi, SeekersGuidance)
Says a room people routinely walk into, or with a window, is not seclusion; suggests an open door, glass room or third colleague
Says work or study emails and messages are fine and flirting is not; Tirmidhi 2165 is cited in sources
Differences: schools define seclusion differently, e.g. whether one man with two women counts

faq:faq-lif-049.title: Can I keep chatting and gaming online with friends of the opposite sex?
keyPoints: Quotes a Shafi'i SeekersGuidance teacher: unnecessary online gaming and chat with the opposite sex is 'undoubtedly inappropriate'
Says what changes is private closeness with a non-relative of the opposite sex; cites Quran 24:30-31
Suggests moving one-to-one chats into groups and turning off voice chat with strangers

faq:faq-lif-034.title: Do I have to start wearing hijab straight away?
keyPoints: Says the four Sunni schools hold hijab obligatory for adult women; cites Quran 33:59
Cites a SeekersGuidance teacher advising starting right away with a simple style rather than in stages
Cites a 2025 Yaqeen US survey: of women converts who wear hijab, 46% began at conversion, 30% months later, 24% a year or more later
Advises making a safety plan with trusted support first if wearing it could bring danger at home

faq:faq-lif-035.title: Do I have to take off my hijab for my passport, licence or health card photo?
keyPoints: Says Canadian passport photos accept a daily religious head covering if the full face and its edges show with no shadows
Says IRCC biometrics allow asking for a same-gender operator and a privacy curtain
Says Ontario driver's licence and health card photos allow religious headwear that covers no part of the face

faq:faq-lif-036.title: Can men wear a gold wedding band, a gold chain or a silk tie?
keyPoints: Cites Nasa'i 5148 (sahih): gold and silk allowed for women, not men; and Muslim 2067a against wearing silk
Says white gold is still gold, per Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam al-Kawthari (Darul Iftaa Leicester) on SeekersGuidance
Differences: Hanafi allows men only a silver ring under a set weight, not steel or tungsten; other schools not checked
Advises talking to a spouse before removing a gold wedding band and swapping it for a silver one

faq:faq-lif-037.title: Is kosher meat halal?
keyPoints: Says Hanafi and Hanbali require God's name over each animal, Shafi'i treat it as recommended, some Malikis require it only of Muslims
Says a Hanafi SeekersGuidance answer concludes kosher meat can be eaten 'as most contemporary scholars have ruled': confirm this reading
Cites Quran 5:5 (food of the People of the Book); says kosher is not the same as halal, nor always forbidden

faq:faq-lif-038.title: Can I eat cheese made with rennet?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school permits rennet from animals other than pigs (Mawlana Ilyas Patel, SeekersGuidance 2011)
Says other schools are stricter and advises avoiding rennet of unknown source; microbial, vegetable or vegetarian labels are easy
Says do not worry about cheese eaten before you knew

faq:faq-lif-039.title: Do I need to question every restaurant kitchen?
keyPoints: Says no need to investigate every possible cross-contamination; ask when reasonably likely (SeekersGuidance, checked by Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat)
Names shared fryer oil with bacon or battered meat as the main case to ask about
Suggests fish and vegetarian dishes as a fallback when you cannot tell

faq:faq-lif-040.title: I hunt and fish. Can I keep doing it?
keyPoints: Says hunting for food or income is permitted and hunting for sport is not (Shaykh Abdul-Rahim Reasat, SeekersGuidance)
Says a Hanafi answer holds catch-and-release fishing impermissible, even to sharpen skills; keep and eat a legal catch
Check the catch-and-release advice against Canadian fishing rules that require releasing undersized or protected fish
Says the conditions for game to be halal must be learned from a qualified teacher

faq:faq-lif-041.title: Can I keep going to a mixed gym?
keyPoints: Cites SeekersGuidance (Mawlana Ilyas Patel): more God-conscious to avoid mixed gyms; home gym, partner or quiet hours meanwhile
Cites AMJA fatwa 23345 (Dr. Main Khalid Al-Qudah): a gym is like a supermarket; go with a lowered gaze and minimal interaction
Advises not to stop exercising and to ask a teacher which view to follow

faq:faq-lif-042.title: What can I wear to swim or play sport?
keyPoints: Says men cover navel to knee, suggesting three-quarter compression pants for swimming (SeekersGuidance)
Cites Shaykh Anas al-Musa: women may swim with conditions: women-only places preferred, loose non-thin clothing, avoid public changing rooms
Says Ontario's creed policy quotes one school board's phys-ed clothing guidelines as examples

faq:faq-lif-043.title: Can I still watch movies and play video games?
keyPoints: Cites Shaykh Irshaad Sedick: streaming subscriptions are not direct help in sin; lawful content in reasonable limits is fine unless duties suffer
Repeats the Shafi'i SeekersGuidance view that unnecessary gaming or chat with the opposite sex is 'undoubtedly inappropriate'
Suggests turning off voice chat with strangers

faq:faq-lif-044.title: Is it okay to take photos and post them online?
keyPoints: Says contemporary scholars differ; a SeekersGuidance answer (Dr. Muhammad Abu Bakr Badhib) reports views permitting and avoiding photos
Cites AMJA fatwa 22672 (Dr. Ibrahim Dremali): camera photos prohibited except for necessity, need or a recognised interest
Cites AMJA fatwa 79414 (Dr. Salah Al-Sawy): posting personal photos publicly, especially of women, is not permissible
Says no need to delete every photo in a panic; think about privacy before posting about your conversion

faq:faq-lif-045.title: My perfume and deodorant contain alcohol. Do I have to throw them out?
keyPoints: Says non-wine alcohol in toiletries is not ritually impure, so perfumes, creams and deodorants are permitted (Hanafi, Shaykh Faraz Rabbani)
Says avoiding them is more cautious because scholars differ; notes a stricter view in the school; other schools not checked

faq:faq-lif-046.title: Can I keep my piercings?
keyPoints: Says customary ear and nose piercings for women are permitted; others, including men's ear piercings, are not (Hanafi, Shaykh Faraz Rabbani)
Says piercings from before Islam need no panic; ask a teacher, as with a tattoo from before Islam

faq:faq-lif-047.title: Can I dye my hair, and does dye affect wudu?
keyPoints: Says hair dye does not stop wudu or ghusl and dyeing grey hair is recommended (Hanafi, Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam)
Says pure black dye is disputed: many Hanafis forbid it, Imam Abu Yusuf permits it, Mufti Taqi Usmani calls it disliked
Cites Muslim 2102b: change grey hair with something but avoid black

faq:faq-wor-031.title: I became Muslim partway through Ramadan. Do I owe the days I missed?
keyPoints: Says fasts from before the Shahada are not owed and need no make-up
Cites a Shafi'i SeekersGuidance answer: making up the day of conversion is sunnah, not required
Says zakat al-fitr depends on whether the person was Muslim when it became due (Bukhari 1503)
Differences: other schools differ on the conversion day itself, such as stopping eating for the rest of that day

faq:faq-wor-032.title: I broke a Ramadan fast on purpose. What do I owe?
keyPoints: Says a deliberately broken fast is made up (qada), some cases add expiation (kaffarah), and fidyah is something different
Cites Bukhari 1936: expiation for intercourse is freeing a slave, else two consecutive months of fasting, else feeding sixty poor
Differences: Hanafi kaffarah for deliberate eating, drinking or intercourse; Shafi'i for intercourse only, not owed by the woman
Says the Maliki and Hanbali positions are not yet sourced

faq:faq-wor-033.title: My parents are not Muslim and are struggling. Can my zakat go to them?
keyPoints: Says zakat goes only to Muslims (Shaykh Dr. Muhammad Abu Bakr Badhib, quoting Malik and Ahmad), so not to non-Muslim parents
Cites Quran 60:8, Bukhari 2620 (Asma and her mother) and Tirmidhi 658 (charity to relatives counts twice)
Differences: the Quran 9:60 'hearts to be reconciled' route is disputed; Shaykh Faraz Rabbani says the Hanafi school holds it abrogated
Gives only the non-Muslim reason; check whether to add that zakat is not given to one's own parents in any case
preCheckFlags: readMore label 'Zakat guide for beginners' leads with the Arabic term; the same page is labelled 'Yearly charity (zakat) for beginners' elsewhere (naming rule)

faq:faq-lif-050.title: Can I buy car insurance and use my work health benefits?
keyPoints: Cites AMJA 86975 (Shaykh Jamaal Zarabozo): scholars in the West seem to agree the legal minimum of car insurance is permissible
Cites AMJA's 2005 third convention: health insurance by need, employer-provided insurance and government coverage are acceptable
Says optional insurance, including life insurance (not yet sourced), needs a scholar; AMJA calls commercial insurance invalid in principle

faq:faq-wor-034.title: I live in the far north and summer fasts are very long. What do I do?
keyPoints: Says most Muslims fast local Fajr to local sunset however long; unbearable hardship allows breaking and making up (Quran 2:185)
Differences: Dr. Jasser Auda (FCNA site) surveys Makkah/Madinah times, the nearest moderate region or latitude caps, called minority views
Says Ramadan 2027 starts around 7 February (Government of Canada) and falls in 'winter and spring' for years; the next several are mostly winter
Advises stopping the fast at signs of serious dehydration and asking the masjid which summer Fajr timetable it uses

faq:faq-wor-035.title: Can I claim my zakat on my Canadian tax return?
keyPoints: Says zakat given to a registered charity with an official receipt can be claimed via CRA line 34900 (the provincial credit is line 58969)
Says gifts to individuals or non-qualified donees do not count; receipts for zakat al-fitr or fidyah depend on the charity
Advises keeping receipts with tax papers, not in the app; general tax information, not tax advice
preCheckFlags: readMore label 'Zakat guide for beginners' leads with the Arabic term; the same page is labelled 'Yearly charity (zakat) for beginners' elsewhere (naming rule)

faq:faq-rel-001.title: Who counts as close family (mahram) now that my family is not Muslim?
keyPoints: Lists a woman's mahrams: father, sons, brothers, uncles, nephews, father-in-law, husband's sons, stepfather after consummation (Quran 4:23, 24:31)
Says a non-Muslim father, brother, son or uncle is still mahram; cousins, brothers-in-law and step-siblings are not
Differences: a Hanafi answer (source review-needed) allows travel or being alone with a non-Muslim mahram who is not morally corrupt
A Hanafi answer ties stepfather status to raising you, Quran 4:23 to consummation; says mahram never obliges being alone with someone unsafe

faq:faq-rel-002.title: I am attracted to people of the same sex. Can I still be Muslim?
keyPoints: Says an unchosen feeling is not a sin, citing a Yaqeen paper based on Dr. Carl Sharif El-Tobgui (source still review-needed)
Cites Bukhari 6243 to separate desire from act; the hadith counts the self's wishing among figurative zina, so confirm it fits
Says sexual acts outside marriage and same-sex acts are prohibited; no need to announce feelings or take on a label
Cites a Yaqeen Dogma Disrupted podcast guest who sees his desires as part of him, not the whole of who he is

faq:faq-rel-003.title: Who can I talk to privately about same-sex attraction?
keyPoints: Recommends a qualified scholar or a Muslim counsellor such as the Khalil Center for faith-sensitive clinical support
Gives Naseeha 1 (866) 627-3342 (24 hours) and Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868 for age 29 or younger
Gives 911 in danger and 9-8-8 by call or text if you feel hopeless
Advises checking who runs any public or online group, and what it teaches, before sharing
preCheckFlags: Crisis order: Khalil Center, Naseeha and Kids Help Phone come before 911 and 9-8-8; the Naseeha source note says the site lists it after 9-1-1 and 9-8-8

faq:faq-rel-004.title: I keep going back to pornography. Does that make my Islam fake?
keyPoints: Says repeatedly returning to pornography does not make Islam fake; the Shahada stands
Says pornography is prohibited, citing Quran 24:30 and a SeekersGuidance answer on the Hanafi and Shafi'i schools (source review-needed)
Cites Muslim 2749: if people did not sin, Allah would bring people who sin, seek forgiveness and are forgiven
Advises repenting the same day and continuing to pray

faq:faq-rel-005.title: Is masturbation allowed if I cannot marry yet?
keyPoints: Says Hanafi and Shafi'i prohibit masturbation; Islamweb 82271 reports Hanbali forbids it except real necessity (fear of zina or illness)
Cites Bukhari 5066: whoever cannot marry should fast
Says ghusl is needed 'if there was a discharge'; the source ties ghusl to fluid after orgasm, so confirm the wording (not pre-seminal fluid)
Notes a SeekersGuidance four-school claim conflicts with the Hanbali view; Maliki view unchecked; three of four sources are review-needed

faq:faq-rel-006.title: How can I stop, and where can I get help?
keyPoints: Cites Dr. Jibran Khokhar (Yaqeen): accountability software, removing trigger apps, devices in shared spaces; marriage is not a cure
Cites Islamweb fatwa 82271 (source review-needed) for fasting, exercise, good company and avoiding explicit material
Refers to a family doctor, a registered psychotherapist or the Khalil Center if it feels out of control
Warns never to send images or money to someone met online

faq:faq-rel-007.title: What does Islam allow between a husband and wife in private?
keyPoints: Says anal intercourse (Abu Dawud 2162, hasan) and intercourse during menstruation (Quran 2:222) are clearly prohibited
Cites Muslim 1006 (reward in lawful intimacy) and Muslim 1437a (spreading a spouse's secrets); ghusl before prayer
Differences: navel-to-knee barrier in a period for Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i; Hanbali allows all but intercourse; non-Hanafi views rest on summaries
Says a Hanafi answer (source review-needed) holds oral contact permitted but disliked and swallowing impure fluids not allowed

faq:faq-rel-008.title: Does being married mean my spouse can insist on sex?
keyPoints: Cites Criminal Code s. 273.1: consent is voluntary agreement to the specific act at the time, and can be withdrawn at any point
Cites Criminal Code s. 278: a husband or wife can be charged with sexually assaulting their spouse
Gives 911 in danger and ESVA Canada's Getting Help page to find a sexual assault centre
Defers the rights spouses have in Islam to a qualified teacher without giving a ruling

faq:faq-rel-009.title: Is birth control allowed in Islam?
keyPoints: Says temporary birth control is allowed for a valid reason (Dr. Hatem al-Haj, AMJA 83665), based on 'azl in Bukhari 5208-5209
Cites Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah fatwa 6101: husband and wife should both agree
Differences: AMJA 83770 says an IUD is permissible whenever birth control is indicated, whatever its duration
Refers to a family doctor and SOGC's Sex and U site for methods; all three fatwa sources are review-needed

faq:faq-rel-010.title: What about sterilisation or abortion?
keyPoints: Cites Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah fatwa 6101 (source review-needed): permanent birth control that ends fertility is not permitted
Gives no ruling on abortion and says no scholarly source on abortion was reviewed; refers to a scholar privately and soon
Says abortion is legal and publicly funded in Canada, per SOGC

faq:faq-rel-011.title: Can a Muslim man have more than one wife in Canada?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 4:3 (up to four wives on condition of justice, else one) and 4:129 (full emotional fairness is not possible)
Says polygamy is a crime in Canada even with only a religious ceremony, and officiants or helpers can be charged (Criminal Code s. 293)
Says a religious-only marriage is not a legal marriage in Canada and lacks a registered marriage's protection
Advises treating a suitor's vagueness or secrecy about an existing marriage as a red flag

faq:faq-rel-012.title: I was sexually assaulted or abused. Is it my sin, and where can I get help?
keyPoints: Says an assaulted person bears no sin because coercion lifts accountability (Shaykh Faraz Rabbani, SeekersGuidance; source review-needed)
Cites Ibn Majah 2045 (sahih): Allah has forgiven what people are forced to do
Says abuse is not a punishment from Allah (Ustadha Shazia Ahmad, SeekersGuidance 2025; source review-needed)
Gives 911 in danger, ESVA Canada's Getting Help page, 9-8-8 any time, and a same-gender counsellor such as the Khalil Center

faq:faq-rel-013.title: I had sexual relationships before Islam. Do I have to tell a future spouse, or get tested?
keyPoints: Says sins before Islam are forgiven, citing Muslim 121 (Islam wipes out what came before it)
Says no scholarly source was found on whether to tell a future spouse; defers to a scholar privately
Says STI testing is a health matter separate from confessing sins; refers to a family doctor, a sexual health clinic and PHAC

faq:faq-rel-014.title: Do I have to cover in front of my spouse, or when I am alone at home?
keyPoints: Cites Ibn Majah 1920 (hasan): guard your awrah except from your spouse; when alone, Allah is more deserving of modesty
Says covering when alone is the more modest choice but 'not the same duty'; confirm, as some schools require covering alone without need
Defers questions about children's privacy and ages at home to a qualified teacher
preCheckFlags: readMore label 'Awrah in the glossary' leads with the Arabic term; the naming rule wants plain English first with the Arabic in brackets

faq:faq-rel-015.title: I have questions about my gender identity. Where do I stand?
keyPoints: Says people are not morally responsible for gender dysphoria they did not choose (Yaqeen paper, Dr. Carl Sharif El-Tobgui; source review-needed)
States as the mainstream position that transitioning socially, with medication or with surgery is not permitted
Gives 911 in danger, 9-8-8 if hopeless, and ESVA's list incl. Trans Lifeline (a US-based peer line): confirm it suits the site
Defers practical questions (such as which prayer row) and post-transition rulings to a qualified scholar privately

faq:faq-fnd-023.title: I had a terrible thought about Allah. Am I still Muslim?
keyPoints: Cites Muslim 132a ('That is the faith manifest') and Bukhari 2528 (thoughts are forgiven unless acted on or spoken)
Says there is no need to say the Shahada again after such thoughts
Tells the reader to say 'Amantu billah' (I believe in Allah); check the transliteration and its citation
Says hours-long intrusive thoughts may be OCD; see a doctor or therapist as well as an imam (CAMH)
preCheckFlags: 'Say Amantu billah' is cited to Bukhari 3276, which only says to seek refuge and stop; the 'amantu billah' wording is in Sahih Muslim 134, which has no source entry

faq:faq-fnd-024.title: I said the Shahada online or on a video call. Does it count?
keyPoints: Says a Shahada said online or by video call is valid (Shaykh Abdurragmaan Khan, SeekersGuidance 2020)
Says repeating it with a local imam is not required but 'undoubtedly desired'
Says a masjid can witness the Shahada later if a certificate is needed, e.g. for a masjid marriage

faq:faq-fnd-025.title: I became Muslim while planning to marry a Muslim. Does my Shahada count?
keyPoints: Quotes Ustadha Shazia Ahmad: 'Marriage being the motivating factor is not a problem', but belief must be real
Cites Nasa'i 3341 (hasan): Abu Talhah became Muslim when proposing to Umm Sulaym, who accepted his Islam as her dowry
Defers whether a particular marriage is valid to a local imam or scholar

faq:faq-fnd-026.title: My partner or their family is pushing me to convert. What should I do?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:256: there is no compulsion in religion
Cites Ustadha Shazia Ahmad: someone who does not truly believe should not say they do; suggests about a year of learning before marrying
Advises talking to an imam not connected to the family, reading the red flags guide, and calling 911 if in danger

faq:faq-fnd-027.title: I have a Bible, a cross or statues from before. What do I do with them?
keyPoints: Says owning books of other religions is not sinful unless reading them may pull you from faith (Ustadh Farid Dingle, SeekersGuidance)
Says no scholarly answer was found for crosses, rosaries, statues or heirlooms; no need to break, burn or discard them before asking
Cites Quran 6:108 (do not insult what others worship); says borrowed items go back to their owner

faq:faq-fnd-028.title: How do I tell what is Islam and what is someone's culture?
keyPoints: Says to ask whether a rule comes from the Quran, the Sunnah or a community's custom; a custom is not an obligation
Cites Bukhari 69: make things easy for people and do not drive them away
Says an online fatwa may not have been written for your situation

faq:faq-fnd-029.title: Are all sins equally serious?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 4:31: if you avoid the major sins, Allah will remove your lesser misdeeds
Cites Bukhari 6857: seven destructive sins, including associating partners with Allah, magic and unlawful killing
Says any sin is a reason to repent, not proof of leaving Islam; a missed Sunnah act is not a major sin

faq:faq-fnd-030.title: Talks about punishment frighten me. How do I hold hope and fear together?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 7:156 ('My mercy encompasses all things') and 39:53 (do not despair of Allah's mercy)
Cites hadith qudsi Bukhari 7405 ('I am just as My slave thinks I am') and Tirmidhi 3540 (hasan: forgiveness nearly as great as the earth)
Advises balancing each talk on punishment with one on mercy and taking anxious questions to a teacher

faq:faq-fnd-031.title: Do I have to follow one school of law (madhhab)?
keyPoints: Says following one madhhab is not a first step; learn one reliable method from one teacher and stay with it
Says the four Sunni schools agree on foundations and differ on details; picking the easiest opinion from each causes trouble
Differences: some scholars present following one recognised school as the norm for a layperson (Yaqeen, Dr. Emad Hamdeh)

faq:faq-fnd-032.title: People at my masjid use labels like Salafi or Sufi. Which one is right?
keyPoints: Says Salafi and Sufi are movements among Sunni Muslims, not separate religions, and you need not join either
Cites the 2005 Amman Message: followers of true Salafi thought and genuine Sufism may not be declared outside Islam
The Amman Message also recognises the Ja'fari and Zaydi Shia schools: confirm it suits the site's mainstream Sunni source rule
Advises stepping back from a group that calls most Muslims not real Muslims or asks you to cut people off

faq:faq-pry-028.title: Someone said my prayer is wrong. What should I do?
keyPoints: Says many corrections, such as where the hands rest, are recognised differences between the schools
Advises thanking the person, staying calm and checking with a teacher before changing anything

faq:faq-fnd-033.title: Two websites give different answers. Can I pick the one I like?
keyPoints: Says you may not choose between scholarly answers by preference, and always taking the strictest is not the test either
Says a fatwa answers one person's situation; note each answer's author and school and ask your teacher

faq:faq-sup-022.title: People at the masjid treat me as less of a Muslim because of my race or background. Is this Islam?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 49:13: nations and tribes were made to know one another; the most noble is the most righteous
Says prejudice among some Muslims comes from culture, not the religion (Yaqeen, Dr. Jonathan A.C. Brown)
Advises writing down what happened, trying another masjid or a convert programme, and reporting threats or harassment

faq:faq-lif-051.title: People say I must convert my family or it will be on me. Is that true?
keyPoints: Says a convert is not accountable for converting family; cites Quran 28:56 (Allah guides whom He wills) and 2:256
Says your part is kindness, answering questions and dua; you can say no to debates and to bringing family to events
Says no ruling is stated on the duty to invite others to Islam

faq:faq-lif-052.title: Can I inherit from my parents who are not Muslim?
keyPoints: Says the four schools allow no fixed-share inheritance across religion, citing Bukhari 6764 ('A Muslim cannot be the heir of a disbeliever')
Says a minority (Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Ibn Taymiyyah) lets a Muslim inherit from a non-hostile non-Muslim (IslamWeb 189195)
Says a bequest in a non-Muslim parent's will to a Muslim is valid in both views
Advises not accepting or refusing anything in the first days after a death; see a scholar and a lawyer

faq:faq-lif-053.title: Can I leave anything to my family who are not Muslim?
keyPoints: Says non-Muslim family can receive lifetime gifts and a bequest from the one-third portion of the will (Bukhari 2742)
Cites Quran 4:11: the fixed shares are divided after bequests and debts
Advises a lawyer to check the will is valid in the reader's province

faq:faq-fnd-034.title: A relative who was not Muslim has died. What do I say to my family, and is it wrong to grieve?
keyPoints: Cites Bukhari 1303: the Prophet wept when his son died and said the heart grieves
Says customary condolences to non-Muslim family are allowed (Hanafi, Tabraze Azam, SeekersGuidance)
Suggests a sample condolence line and says never tell grieving relatives where their loved one will end up

faq:faq-fnd-035.title: Can I pray for my parent who died without being Muslim?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 9:113 on not asking forgiveness for polytheists once it is clear they are bound for the Fire
Says many scholars (SeekersGuidance) allow no formal prayer for forgiveness but allow hope and asking that they receive what is best
Cites Dar al-Ifta al-Misriyyah fatwa 5934: a child may ask forgiveness for a parent who may not have received the message properly

faq:faq-fnd-036.title: Will my family who are not Muslim go to Hell? What can I pray for them?
keyPoints: Says Muslims do not declare any individual's fate; cites Quran 17:15 (no punishment until a messenger reaches them)
Cites Dr. Jonathan Brown (Yaqeen) on al-Ghazali's test of hearing about Islam reliably and accurately
Cites Bukhari 2937: the Prophet prayed for the guidance of Daws instead of cursing them
Differences: Maturidi view that reason alone makes a person responsible for believing in a Creator; others: none without revelation

faq:faq-lif-054.title: Can a Muslim foster or adopt a child in Canada?
keyPoints: Says kafalah keeps the child's link to the birth family; FCNA/AMJA guideline keeps the birth family name as a last or middle name
Says mahram rules apply from puberty and a child in care can receive up to one third of the estate by will
Differences: FCNA calls five feedings unanimous; the site says Shafi'i/Hanbali count five and Hanafi/Maliki any feeding in two years
Advises a scholar and a family lawyer because provincial adoption law may work differently

faq:faq-lif-055.title: I adopted a child before I became Muslim. Do I need to change anything?
keyPoints: Says an adopted child stays yours to love and care for; do not undo anything in a hurry
Says rules may apply over time: birth family name as middle or last name where possible, and mahram rules after puberty (FCNA)
Says provide for the child through the one-third portion of the will, with a scholar and a family lawyer together

faq:faq-pry-029.title: I am Deaf, blind, autistic or have an intellectual disability. What does Islam ask of me?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 2:286: what is asked follows what a person can do; worship need not be physically identical to others'
Recommends Deaf Muslims of Canada for ASL interpreters at events; its religious orientation and charity status are not stated
Recommends ISDHH, a US group, for ASL classes and khutbah interpretation: confirm it is suitable

faq:faq-fnd-037.title: What do SAW, PBUH, SWT, RA and AS mean?
keyPoints: Gives transliterations and meanings: sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, subhanahu wa ta'ala, alayhis-salam, radiyallahu anhu/anha, rahimahullah
Says the blessing on the Prophet rests on Quran 33:56 and the RA wording comes from Quran 9:100
Says AS is usually said after other prophets (Jesus, Moses, Abraham) and angels such as Gabriel

faq:faq-fnd-038.title: Do I have to say "peace be upon him" every time, and is writing PBUH wrong?
keyPoints: Says say the blessing on hearing or reading the Prophet's name, 'quietly or in your heart': confirm the heart alone suffices
Cites Tirmidhi 3546 (hasan sahih gharib per at-Tirmidhi): the one who hears his name and sends no blessing is stingy
Says Imam al-Nawawi recommended writing the blessing in full; a Hanafi mufti (Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam) advises against SAW
Says nobody should shame PBUH in a quick message; the site writes 'peace be upon him' in English

faq:faq-fnd-039.title: Who counts as a shaykh or a mufti, and who should I ask about my own life?
keyPoints: Cites Qalam Institute (US) usage: shaykh (graduate with years of teaching), mufti (licensed to give fatwas), ustadh (graduate starting to teach)
Says there is no go-between in Islam, so no imam is needed to pray or repent (New Muslim Guide source is review-needed)
Advises asking an imam or scholar tied to an established masjid or institute, and asking where they studied

faq:faq-lrn-011.title: Is my prayer valid if I mispronounce words?
keyPoints: Says a trying learner's prayer is valid in most cases despite mispronunciation; correct a word once, do not restart over one letter
Cites Muslim 798a: the one who recites with difficulty gets a double reward
Differences: Shafi'i (Reliance f18.8) invalid only if meaning changes and it was deliberate; Hanafi (Ibn Abidin) excuses a saad/seen mix-up

faq:faq-lrn-012.title: What do I do with an old or damaged Quran?
keyPoints: Says readable copies are kept or passed on; unreadable pages may be buried where no one walks, shredded or burned respectfully
Differences: Hanafi SeekersGuidance answer (Ibn Abidin) prefers burial and allows shredding; Islamweb 510508 allows burial or burning
Cites Uthman's order to burn other written Quran materials (Bukhari 4987) as precedent; says never put a Quran in recycling

faq:faq-pry-031.title: A dog licked my hand, or my baby wet my shirt. Can I still pray?
keyPoints: Says most impurity is washed until its substance, colour and smell are gone as far as reasonably possible
Cites Bukhari 223: water was poured over a milk-fed baby boy's urine without further washing
Cites Muslim 279a (dog-licked vessel washed seven times); says the Shafi'i school treats dog saliva as heavy impurity, one wash with earth

faq:faq-pry-032.title: My family does the laundry, and I found a spot after I prayed. Is my prayer okay?
keyPoints: Says machine-washed clothes with no trace of filth can be taken as clean; no need to rewash a relative's loads (Hanafi)
Says a small underwear mark found after prayer, absent at wudu, needs no repeat of the prayer (Hanafi, Tabraze Azam)
Says a doubt on its own does not make anything impure (Bukhari 137 in sources)

faq:faq-pry-030.title: My perfume, deodorant or hand sanitiser contains alcohol. Can I pray wearing it?
keyPoints: Says non-wine alcohol is not ritually impure and can be used on the body (Hanafi, Shaykh Faraz Rabbani), implying prayer wearing it is valid
Says avoiding it is more cautious because some scholars, including within the Hanafi school, are stricter

faq:faq-pry-042.title: How do Muslims clean themselves after using the toilet? Is toilet paper enough?
keyPoints: Says paper then water is best, and paper alone meets the basic sunnah while the impurity stays at the exit (Hanafi, SeekersGuidance)
Says washing with water is required if impurity spreads beyond the exit and the area right around it
Advises using the left hand, cleaning once properly and ignoring doubts; Muslim 262a on toilet etiquette is in sources
Differences: the schools differ on facing the qibla in a washroom inside a building

faq:faq-pry-043.title: I wear a headscarf. Do I have to take it off for wudu at work?
keyPoints: Says the Hanafi school requires wiping at least a quarter of the head itself; wiping over the scarf does not count
Says the Hanbali school allows wiping a scarf wrapped under the chin, put on in wudu, for a day and night (three when travelling)
Cites Mawlana Ilyas Patel: one may follow the Hanbali view if the wudu and the prayer are both valid in that school
Says the Shafi'i and Maliki sources were not checked; mentions wiping over suitable socks
preCheckFlags: readMore label 'Wudu and ghusl guide' leads with Arabic terms; the site's own nav calls this page 'Washing before prayer (wudu and ghusl)' (naming rule)

faq:faq-pry-033.title: Do women have to go to Friday prayer?
keyPoints: Cites Abu Dawud 1067 (sahih, al-Albani): Friday prayer is not obligatory on women, children, the sick or slaves; a Hanafi text adds travellers
Says if a woman attends, Jumu'ah takes the place of Dhuhr that day
Says 'Missing Jumu'ah is nothing to feel guilty about' without limiting that sentence to women; check it cannot be read as general

faq:faq-pry-034.title: Friday prayer falls in my work hours. What should I do?
keyPoints: Says Friday prayer is an obligation for adult men, citing Quran 62:9
Says Canadian human rights law protects religion (modified hours as an example); the CHRC guide cited covers only federally regulated employers
Cites a Hanafi answer (Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam): not permitted to take a job where you regularly cannot attend Friday prayer

faq:faq-pry-035.title: I'm driving a long way to see family. Do I shorten my prayers?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 4:101; says Dhuhr, Asr and Isha become two rak'ahs, while Fajr and Maghrib stay the same
Says Hanafi: a trip of at least about 77 km and a stay under 15 days, and shortening is then required
Says Shafi'i: more than about 79 to 80 km past the city limits and a stay under four days, not counting travel days
Differences: schools differ on distance, stay, obligation and combining; AMJA (fatwa 3078) gives no fixed number of days

faq:faq-pry-036.title: How do I pray on a plane?
keyPoints: Says pray on a flight when the time comes in, and stand, bow and prostrate if there is space (Hanafi, Shaykh Faraz Rabbani)
Says a prayer prayed seated with head movements must be repeated after landing
Says face the qibla as best you can and shorten four-rak'ah prayers if the flight counts as travel
preCheckFlags: Attributes 'repeat a seated prayer on landing' to the linked Hanafi answer, but its source note says repeating a seated prayer is not covered there

faq:faq-pry-037.title: I slept through Fajr again. What now?
keyPoints: Cites Muslim 681: there is no negligence in sleep; pray when you become aware of it
Cites Muslim 684a: a forgotten prayer is prayed when remembered, with nothing else owed
Says oversleeping does not make you a hypocrite; the practical tips are labelled as not rulings

faq:faq-pry-038.title: I work night shifts or long hospital shifts. Can I combine prayers?
keyPoints: Cites AMJA fatwas 79663 and 22038: combining for real work hardship is allowed as a temporary measure, not a daily habit
Cites Muslim 705a: the Prophet combined prayers in Madinah without fear or travel
Says the Hanafi school allows only praying at the end of one time and the start of the next, or fully following another school

faq:faq-pry-039.title: Is it okay to pray at the very end of the prayer time?
keyPoints: Says a prayer anywhere inside its time counts, and one prayed before its time has begun does not
Cites Bukhari 527: prayer at its time is the deed Allah loves most (the source notes the English adds 'early')
Says do not leave Asr until the sun turns yellow; Hanafi prefers Fajr once the sky is light and delaying Isha

faq:faq-pry-040.title: Do I need a prayer mat or special clothes to pray?
keyPoints: Says any clean surface works; men cover at least navel to knee and women all but face and hands, including hair (Abu Dawud 641)
Differences: Hanafi leaves a woman's feet uncovered in prayer (covering advised); Hanbali asks a man to cover a shoulder (Bukhari 359)

faq:faq-pry-041.title: My compass was a few degrees off from the qibla. Do I need to pray again?
keyPoints: Says a prayer a few degrees off the qibla need not be repeated; the general direction is enough when you cannot be exact
Cites Quran 2:144 and Tirmidhi 344 (sahih, Darussalam): 'What is between the east and the west is qibla', applied to those far away

faq:faq-sup-023.title: Someone harassed me because I am Muslim. What should I do?
keyPoints: Says call 911 if hurt or in danger; then write down what happened and save screenshots or photos before deleting anything
Gives Crime Stoppers 1-800-222-8477 for anonymous reports, local police and NCCM's incident form
Says being targeted is not your fault and feeling shaken afterwards is common

faq:faq-sup-024.title: Is it worth reporting if it was only words and nobody was hurt?
keyPoints: Says the RCMP treats a slur or mocking religion online as a hate incident even when not a crime, and says reporting helps
Cites Statistics Canada (2019 survey): only 22% of incidents seen as hate-motivated were reported to police
Says NCCM does not share your information without your consent

faq:faq-sup-026.title: I drink or use drugs and keep slipping. Where can I get help?
keyPoints: Says ask a doctor before stopping heavy daily drinking because CAMH says alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous
Points to provincial and territorial addiction lines listed by the Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction
Cites Bukhari 6780: the Prophet forbade cursing a companion repeatedly punished for drinking, as he loved Allah and His Messenger
Says a slip does not end your Islam; repent and start again the same day

faq:faq-pry-044.title: I am not sure whether my wudu broke. Do I need to make it again?
keyPoints: Says wudu still stands when you are only unsure whether it broke; certainty is not removed by a doubt
Cites Bukhari 137: do not leave the prayer unless you hear a sound or notice a smell
Points readers with many daily doubts to the section on doubts that will not stop
preCheckFlags: Differences says the schools share the rule, but the Maliki relied-upon view (Mukhtasar Khalil) is that doubting wudu after known purity requires wudu, except chronic doubters

faq:faq-sup-027.title: I keep repeating wudu and get thoughts about Allah that I hate. Am I losing my faith?
keyPoints: Cites Muslim 132a: hated intrusive thoughts are 'the faith manifest', not a loss of faith
Says repeated wudu and unwanted thoughts can be OCD; attributes fear of blasphemous thoughts and excessive washing to CAMH
Says OCD is treatable, most often with CBT (CAMH also mentions medication); see a doctor and follow one teacher's simple standard

faq:faq-sup-025.title: The first weeks felt amazing. Now I feel nothing when I pray. Was I ever sincere?
keyPoints: Says feeling flat after the first months is common and does not mean the conversion was fake
Cites Muslim 2750a: Hanzala feared hypocrisy when his feeling of faith faded at home, and the Prophet reassured him
Cites Bukhari 6464: the deeds most beloved to Allah are the regular ones, even if small
Says talk to a doctor if low mood lasts most of the day for more than two weeks (CAMH depression criteria)

faq:faq-sup-002.title: There is so much to learn. How do I keep from feeling overwhelmed?
keyPoints: Recommends New Muslim Academy self-paced courses and forums: confirm it is mainstream Sunni and suitable
Advises learning one thing at a time, usually prayer first; Bukhari 39 (the religion is easy) is in sources

faq:faq-sup-028.title: I drifted away from Islam for a while. Can I come back?
keyPoints: Cites Quran 39:53: do not lose hope in Allah's mercy, for He forgives all sins
Says the four schools' relied-upon positions require making up missed prayers; some scholars differed on prayers missed on purpose
Advises a gentle make-up plan with a teacher (one source is review-needed); says nobody at the masjid is owed an explanation
Does not address someone who left Islam outright (renewing the Shahada, prayers missed while outside Islam)

faq:faq-sup-029.title: My family and old friends pulled away after I converted. Why does it feel like grief?
keyPoints: Cites psychotherapists Najwa Awad and Sarah Sultan (Yaqeen): grief follows losses besides death and is not a sign of weak faith
Says the Prophet wept when his son Ibrahim died, supported only through the Yaqeen article (which cites Bukhari 1303)
Suggests a counsellor if sadness stays heavy 'for months'; faq-sup-025 uses CAMH's two-week threshold for seeing a doctor

faq:faq-sup-030.title: I have had thoughts of ending my life. What should I do?
keyPoints: Gives 911 for immediate danger first, then 9-8-8 by call or text any time, day or night, in English or French
Says these thoughts show how much pain you carry and you deserve care, not blame; tell one person you trust today
Check 'Your faith and professional help can go together' against the rule keeping clinical and religious guidance in separate sentences
